title: Slot efficiency & microburst daily breakdown (APAC/EU/NA) — Week Apr 25–May 1, 2026
summary: Export from internal grafana dashboard (slot-occupancy + microburst detector). Goal: quantify how short, high-amplitude slot churn (microbursts) interacts with avg slot utilization to affect tail latency and preemption rates across pools and regions for the week Apr 25–May 1, 2026.
methodology: Samples: 5-minute slot occupancy snapshots; microburst defined as >=20% absolute change in used_slots within a single 1-minute interpolation window; tail latency measured as p95 of token write latency from runtime traces. Aggregation: per-cluster, per-pool daily aggregates plus weekly summary.
key_findings: Spot/spot-like pools (apac spot-pool & dev-pool) show highest microburst frequency and the largest p95 tail latencies when avg utilization is between 40-60%.
Prod pools with H100 capacity maintain lower p95 latencies at high utilization (>75%) unless microburst count spikes >20 events/day.
Preemptions correlate strongly with burst events in APAC clusters (r~0.72) — likely due to autoscaler knob and spot eviction noise.
Avg batch size increases in high-util clusters (prod-pool NA) and masks some microburst-induced latency, but increases per-token cost.
A small number of short high-amplitude bursts (>=50% slot change) account for disproportionate p95 increases on dev/test clusters — candidate for local prefix caching or smoother scale-up policy.
notes:
Quick raw observations:
- Apr 30 (APAC dev) shows extreme tail (220ms) tied to 61 burst events; correlated with a scheduled CI load spike. Need to verify CI gating on APAC clusters.
- EU dev (Apr 25) p95 84ms despite high avg 72% — bursts smaller amplitude but frequent; investigate autoscaler vertical scaling threshold.
- NA prod steady but observe two mid-week burst clusters (Apr 26 & May 1) that line up with large canary rollouts (see linked deployment IDs).
recommended_actions: Add a short (60s) smoothing window in the spot autoscaler to reduce 1-minute microburst reactions for dev/spot pools.
Add targeted prefix caching for dev/test pools that experience frequent small bursts to reduce p95 impact without increasing dedicated capacity.
Lift telemetry retention for microburst traces by +7 days for affected clusters to help root cause (JIRA-ENG-INFRA-842).
Evaluate moving some non-critical CI traffic off apac-1 during peak maintenance windows (follow-up with solutions-engineering).
open_questions: Can we reduce scheduled CI concurrency on APAC pools without impacting dev velocity?
Are there specific model families in spot pools that amplify burst sensitivity (e.g., long-sequence chat workloads)?
Do current preemption signals from cloud provider align with our burst detector time windows (need cloud team input)?
